canonical_title: Vertical axis response in hovering flight
subject_group: 6.1.10 Vertical/short takeoff and landing air vehicles

versions.title_at_revision: Vertical axis response in hovering flight
versions.text: Criterion: Verify safe vertical axis response in hovering flight. Standard: The air vehicle meets the standards within MIL-STD-1797, 5.2.7.2.1.4 Vertical axis response in hovering flight (see table XCIV for guidance). Method of Compliance: Verification methods include analysis, test, demonstration, simulation, and inspection of process, design, test, or configuration documentation.

versions.title_at_revision: Vertical axis response in hovering flight
versions.text:
Standard: The air vehicle is no worse than Level 2 as specified in MIL-STD-1797, Vertical Axis Response in Hovering Flight paragraph, unless pilot evaluation determines the air vehicle handling qualities are no worse than Level 2. Method of Compliance: Prior to entering flight test, verify the standard by the following method(s): Analysis.
(1) Conduct analysis of hover vertical velocity response to evaluate air vehicle capabilities for all required hover loadings and configurations, ensuring an allocation of thrust margin is available for control margin for all 3 rotational axes in hover, to include: a. Baseline control system. b. Precision hover modes. Vertical velocity response analysis IGE should be IAW program requirements, which typically include VLs and VTOs, but typically not height captures IGE. Test.
  (1) Lab test: Conduct piloted simulation and evaluation to assess flying/handling qualities as specified in MIL-STD-1797, Vertical Takeoff (VTO) paragraph, Vertical Landing (VL) paragraph, and specifically, waveoff maneuvers and height stabilize maneuvers during VLs for each combination of air vehicle states, control modes, and environmental conditions, to include: a. Baseline control system. b. Precision hover modes. Pilot will assess overall workload, pilot compensation, and any undesirable coupling of thrust commands into other axes. Pilot will assess timeliness of h-dot response and height lost during a stabilize or waveoff maneuver from a nominal descent rate VL IAW program requirements. Prior to entering operational test/operations, verify the standard by the above and following method(s): Test.
  (2) Flight test: Conduct flight test to assess flying/handling qualities as specified in MIL-STD- 1797, Vertical Takeoff (VTO) paragraph, Vertical Landing (VL) paragraph, and specifically, waveoff maneuvers and height stabilize maneuvers during VLs for selected combinations of air vehicle states, control modes, and environmental conditions, to include: a. Baseline control system. b. Precision hover modes. Pilot will assess overall workload, pilot compensation, and any undesirable coupling of thrust commands into other axes. Pilot will assess timeliness of h-dot response and height lost during a stabilize or waveoff maneuver from a nominal descent rate VL IAW program requirements.
